record.original_question: Can we avoid long abelian cubes over two letters?

evidence.quote: Can we avoid long abelian cubes over two letters?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma=\{0,1\}$ be a binary alphabet. A finite nonempty word $w\in\Sigma^+$ is called an abelian cube if it can be written as $w=xyz$ with $|x|=|y|=|z|\ge 1$ and the three factors $x,y,z$ are pairwise abelian-equivalent, i.e. each letter of $\Sigma$ occurs the same number of times in $x$, in $y$, and in $z$. The common length $|x|$ is called the period of the abelian cube.

An infinite word $\mathbf{w}\in\Sigma^{\mathbb N}$ is said to avoid long abelian cubes if there exists an integer $N\ge 1$ such that no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is an abelian cube of period at least $N$.

Question: Does there exist an integer $N$ and an infinite binary word $\mathbf{w}\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ such that $\mathbf{w}$ contains no abelian cube $xyz$ with $|x|\ge N$? Equivalently, can long abelian cubes be avoided over a two-letter alphabet?
artifact.status_search_result: The exact original question on avoiding long abelian cubes over a binary alphabet (in the sense of an absolute lower bound on the period) appears not to have a definitive published resolution under that exact formulation; however, several closely related strengthenings have been proved. Mercaş and Saarela (DLT 2013) showed that 3-abelian cubes are avoidable on a binary alphabet, and Rao subsequently strengthened this to show that 2-abelian cubes are avoidable on a binary alphabet. These results give partial progress in the direction of avoiding abelian cubes with long factors, but the literal "long abelian cube" avoidability problem on two letters in the period-bounded form has not been clearly settled in the sources retrieved.

status_evidence.title: 3-Abelian Cubes Are Avoidable on Binary Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Previously it has been known that k-abelian cubes are avoidable over a binary alphabet for k ≥ 5; here it is proved that this holds for k ≥ 3.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: 3-abelian cubes (a stronger notion) are avoidable on two letters.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions (Mercaş, Rao, Saarela).
status_evidence.claim: Closely related work studying avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions, including binary cases.

status_evidence.title: 5-Abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier result that 5-abelian cubes are avoidable on a binary alphabet, later improved.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier partial step toward avoiding long abelian-like cubes over two letters.
